saints.name: Pope St. Felix I
saints.title: Pope
saints.shortBlurb: A pope of the third century who governed the Roman Church in a time of peace between persecutions…
biography: Felix succeeded St. Dionysius as bishop of Rome early in 269, under the Emperor Aurelian. In that year the synod of Antioch that deposed Paul of Samosata for heresy addressed its report to Rome, and a letter sent eastward under Felix's name expounded the doctrine of the Trinity against the error.

Only a fragment of that letter survives, interpolated by an Apollinarist hand and read at the Council of Ephesus in 431. The Liber Pontificalis further credits Felix with decreeing that Mass be celebrated over the tombs of the martyrs, though this more likely mirrors the custom of his day than any ordinance of his own.

Later legend made Felix a martyr, confusing him with a Roman namesake buried on the Via Aurelia, but the ancient Depositio episcoporum lists him among the bishops, not the martyrs. He died in 274 and was buried on 30 December in the catacomb of St. Callixtus on the Appian Way, where the calendar of 354 keeps his memory.
saints.knownFor: A third-century pope of the Roman Church under Aurelian.
